name: Bicephal Wyrmhole
biography: Hypergravitas bicephalis. A two-headed gravity-warping aberration that drinks light (AC 18 in Bright Light thanks to its Distortion Armour's Three-Quarters Cover), drags everything into its well, and switches gravity off entirely before slamming it back on. Habitat: Hill & Mountain.

features.name: Consume Chroma
features.description: Whenever the bicephal wyrmhole is subjected to Radiant damage, it regains Hit Points equal to the Radiant damage dealt.

features.name: Distortion Armour
features.description: The bicephal wyrmhole bends light around it in strange ways, making it difficult to track visually. While in Bright Light, the bicephal wyrmhole has Three-Quarters Cover (AC 18). A Blinded creature, or one that closes its eyes or does not rely on sight, ignores this cover.

features.name: Gravity Well
features.description: The area within 10 feet of the bicephal wyrmhole is Difficult Terrain for creatures other than bicephal wyrmholes.

features.name: Multiattack
features.description: The bicephal wyrmhole makes one Stinger attack and one Warping Blade attack.

features.name: Stinger
features.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) Psychic damage. Saving Throw: DC 15 Wisdom, a creature hit by this attack. Failure: The target is disoriented and immediately uses its Reaction to move a distance equal to its Speed in a random direction.

features.name: Warping Blade
features.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Force damage. Each creature within 5 feet of the target takes 4 (1d8) Force damage.

features.name: Gravity Suspension (Recharge 5-6)
features.description: The bicephal wyrmhole disables gravity around it. Creatures and objects within 60 feet of it come under the effects of the Levitate spell and rise 15 feet into the air if not tethered to the ground. At the start of the bicephal wyrmhole's next turn, gravity rapidly intensifies, and creatures without a Fly Speed or that otherwise aren't held aloft fall to the ground. Double the fall distance when calculating damage from falling in this way.
